Democrats have seized control of both the House and Senate in a devastating midterm election blow to Donald Trump, as a 'blue tsunami' sweeps across America. In a stunning political upset, Democrats flipped Senate seats in traditionally Republican strongholds, with James Talarico defeating Trump-backed Ken Paxton in Texas, South Carolina electing its first Democratic senator since 1998, and Kansas sending a Democrat to the Senate for the first time since 1932. Democrats also claimed major victories in Iowa and Ohio. The results represent a dramatic rejection of Trump’s second-term agenda, with exit polls suggesting frustration over the cost of living played a major role. With Democrats now controlling both chambers of Congress, Trump faces two years of legislative gridlock, potential investigations into his administration and even the prospect of a third impeachment. #Midterms2026 #DonaldTrump #Democrats #BlueTsunami #USPolitics

Here’s what happened in America in the last 12 hours. Democrats have won control of both chambers of the United States Congress, delivering a major midterm setback to President Donald Trump and Republicans. James Talarico has won Texas’s United States Senate race, becoming the first Democrat elected to the seat since nineteen eighty-eight, according to projections. After the United States midterm losses, President Donald Trump said he would work with Democrats but veto legislation he opposes. Democrat Troy Jackson has defeated Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine, ending her nearly thirty-year tenure in the United States Senate. Democrat Adam Hamilton has defeated incumbent Republican Roger Marshall in Kansas, flipping a United States Senate seat previously held by Republicans. Democrat Sherrod Brown is returning to the United States Senate after defeating Republican Jon Husted in Ohio, according to NBC News projections. Former North Carolina governor Roy Cooper has defeated Republican Michael Whatley, flipping a United States Senate seat for Democrats in a major upset. Democrat Chris Pappas has defeated former senator John Sununu in New Hampshire, retaining the United States Senate seat for his party. Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff has defeated Republican Mike Collins in Georgia, keeping his United States Senate seat in Democratic hands. Republican Senator Pete Ricketts has won re-election in Nebraska, defeating independent challenger Dan Osborn, according to projections from major broadcasters. Republican Ashley Moody has defeated Democrat Angie Nixon in Florida’s United States Senate special election, keeping the seat under Republican control. Democrat Gina Hinojosa has defeated Republican Greg Abbott in Texas’s governor race, ending his tenure and flipping the state’s governorship. Democrat Denise Powell has won Nebraska’s second congressional district, replacing retiring Republican Representative Don Bacon in the United States House. Here’s what happened in America in the last 12 hours. None of the U.S. House Republicans who voted to impeach President Donald Trump over January sixth will return to Congress next year. U.S. Vice-President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican midterm defeat, while Trump also acknowledged the conflict contributed to losses. Elon Musk spent nearly five hundred million dollars backing Republicans in the U.S. midterms, but his spending failed to prevent major Democratic victories. U.S. stock markets rallied after Democrats won Congress, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average gaining nearly sixteen hundred points in one day. Indiana carried out its first U.S. execution of the year, putting Jeffrey Weisheit to death ahead of two other executions scheduled Thursday. A shooting at the Citibank campus in Florida left two people dead, including the suspected gunman, while four others suffered injuries. Mississippi’s U.S. Senate race remained undecided, with Democrat Scott Colom narrowly leading Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith as officials counted outstanding ballots. Democrat Eric Armstrong won an Iowa state legislative seat despite withdrawing from the U.S. election race before voting day. Democrat Amish Shah defeated Republican Jay Feely in Arizona, flipping the U.S. House seat and strengthening the party’s congressional majority. Democrats plan to pursue healthcare changes in the U.S. Congress, including restoring expired insurance subsidies and reversing cuts to Medicaid funding. President Trump urged the U.S. Congress to pass legislation making daylight saving time permanent, ending seasonal clock changes nationwide. In these midterm elections, which occurred during the second term of Republican president Donald Trump, all 435 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 seats in the U.S. Senate were contested to determine the 120th United States Congress. Thirty-nine state and territorial U.S. gubernatorial elections, attorney general elections, and numerous state and local elections were also contested. As of November 4, the Democratic Party is projected to have won a majority of seats in both houses of Congress, and won numerous other offices currently held by Republicans. #america #usa #midterms #2026 #edit
